items.followUp: What is the difference between soluble and insoluble dietary fibre?

rubric.why: Identifies insoluble dietary fibre as indigestible plant material or names a valid example.
rubric.description: Insoluble dietary fibres are indigestible plant materials, such as cellulose.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying fibre as indigestible plant material or naming cellulose.

rubric.why: States the defining property of insoluble fibre.
rubric.description: These fibres do not dissolve in water.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the fibres are insoluble in water.

modelAnswer: Insoluble dietary fibres are indigestible plant materials, such as cellulose.
They do not dissolve in water.

items.followUp: Name and briefly describe five careers related to biology.

rubric.why: Identifies two biology-related careers and gives their roles.
rubric.description: Medicine involves diagnosing and treating diseases; agriculture uses biology to grow and improve crops.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for each of the two careers identified with an appropriate role.

rubric.why: Identifies two further biology-related careers and gives their roles.
rubric.description: Animal husbandry applies biology to breeding and caring for farm animals; fisheries includes fish farming and management.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for each of the two careers identified with an appropriate role.

rubric.why: Identifies a fifth biology-related career and gives its role.
rubric.description: Forestry concerns managing and conserving forests.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying forestry and its role.

modelAnswer: Medicine: biologists can become doctors who diagnose and treat diseases.
Agriculture: biology is used to grow and improve crops.
Animal husbandry: biology is applied to breeding and caring for farm animals.
Fisheries: biologists work in fish breeding, fish farming and fisheries management.
Forestry: biologists help manage and conserve forests.

items.followUp: Describe five ways in which deforestation can affect the environment.

rubric.why: Names two effects of removing trees on soil and water flow.
rubric.description: Deforestation increases soil erosion and can increase the risk of floods.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for each effect identified.

rubric.why: Names two effects of deforestation on climate and ecosystems.
rubric.description: Deforestation contributes to global warming and reduces biodiversity by destroying habitats.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for each effect identified.

rubric.why: Names an effect of deforestation on the water cycle or rainfall.
rubric.description: Deforestation disrupts the water cycle and can reduce rainfall.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying this effect.

modelAnswer: Deforestation increases soil erosion because tree roots no longer hold the soil together.
It can increase the risk of floods.
It contributes to global warming and climate change.
It destroys habitats and reduces biodiversity, and may lead to species extinction.
It disrupts the water cycle and can reduce rainfall, causing drought or desertification.

items.followUp: Write the balanced equation for photosynthesis and state the conditions needed for it.

rubric.why: Explains that photosynthesis uses light energy to make glucose from carbon dioxide and water.
rubric.description: Green plants use light energy to make glucose from carbon dioxide and water.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating the basic process with its reactants and product.

rubric.why: Includes the correct reactants and products in the equation.
rubric.description: Carbon dioxide and water form glucose and oxygen.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct reactants and products.

rubric.why: Gives the balanced chemical equation for photosynthesis.
rubric.description: The balanced equation has coefficients 6, 6, 1 and 6.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the balanced equation.

rubric.why: Identifies both the energy source and the pigment required for photosynthesis.
rubric.description: Sunlight provides energy, which is absorbed by chlorophyll.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming both sunlight or light energy and chlorophyll.

modelAnswer: Photosynthesis is the process by which green plants use light energy to make glucose from carbon dioxide and water, releasing oxygen.
Sunlight provides the energy for the process, and chlorophyll absorbs the light energy.
